podcast.title: Edwin Left 1997 Solo; Brian Byrne Tape Initially Thrown Out, Then Hired; Edwin Returned 2016
podcast.body: I Mother Earth formed when Jagori Tanna and Christian Tanna met Edwin at their shared rehearsal space in 1990, creating a band immediately subject to a major-label bidding war. Edwin left in 1997 to go solo, finishing tour commitments that summer. The following year, auditions began; hundreds of demo tapes arrived, including one from a Newfoundlander named Brian Byrne that was immediately discarded. A mutual friend insisted they look again; Brian got a second chance, got the gig, and served as singer from 1998 to 2003. After a long hiatus, a 2012 reunion brought Brian back; Edwin was invited back again in 2016. Both occasionally share the stage on current tours. "His tape was immediately thrown out."

podcast.title: Brian Byrne's Post-I Mother Earth Career
podcast.body: After the band's initial breakup, Brian Byrne worked in radio in Halifax and made a serious attempt to audition as the new singer for Stone Temple Pilots, though he was not selected. "Brian eventually ended up working as a radio guy in Halifax. He also made a hard run auditioning to be the new singer in Stone Temple Pilots."

podcast.title: Christian Tana's Post-I Mother Earth Career
podcast.body: Christian Tana remained involved in music, collaborating with his brother's record label, and took on roles as the general manager of an event venue in Peterborough and an event planner for a theater in Cobourg, Ontario. "Christian Tana stayed with music, working with his brother's record label, and taking a gig as the general manager of an event venue in Peterborough and working as an event planner for a theater in Coburg, Ontario."

podcast.title: Post-Can Rock Revolution Breakup and Reform
podcast.body: I Mother Earth were among the Canadian bands that broke up after the 1990s but later reformed due to public demand, demonstrating the lasting impact and fan loyalty cultivated during the Can Rock Revolution. "Others broke up, like I'm on the earth, and the real statics and lowest of the low, only to reform later due to public demand."

xref.title: Christian Samson's Post-Band Career
xref.body: Drummer Christian Samson played with Edwin after his departure from I Mother Earth, had brief stints with Moist and the prog rock group Saga, and now manages his own HVAC condo service. This shows a diverse career path both within and outside the music industry. "drummer Christian Samson played around with Edwin after he left I Mother Earth. There was also a short stint in Moist and with saga, the Prague Rock Group, and he's now running his own HVAC condo service."
